root_cause.text: The writeback sync path in `sync_inodes_sb()` wrongly waited for flusher-thread completion for FUSE and other filesystems that cannot provide sync data-integrity guarantees, because the no-data-integrity state was modeled per-inode (`AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY`) and only skipped `wait_sb_inodes()` inode writeback waits, not the earlier superblock-wide `wb_wait_for_completion()`-style flusher wait.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that “mappings with no data integrity guarantees skipped waiting on writeback completion but still waited on the flusher threads to finish initiating the writeback,” causing a suspend-to-RAM hang with stack trace ending in `wb_wait_for_completion` from `sync_inodes_sb`; the patch fixes this by adding `SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY` and making `sync_inodes_sb()` “kick off writeback and return” for such superblocks, while removing the old per-mapping `AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY` logic.

intent_record.intent_summary: Ensure `wait_sb_inodes()` waits on all writeback-tagged mappings instead of incorrectly skipping those without data integrity semantics.
intent_record.what: The change removes the explanatory comment about skipping mappings without data integrity semantics and deletes the `mapping_no_data_integrity(mapping)` condition from the `if` statement, leaving only the `!mapping_tagged(mapping, PAGECACHE_TAG_WRITEBACK)` check to decide whether to continue.
intent_record.how: At runtime, `wait_sb_inodes()` will no longer skip waiting on inodes whose mappings lack data integrity semantics if they are still tagged for writeback; it will wait for their writeback completion whenever the writeback tag is present.

intent_record.intent_summary: Skip waiting for synchronous inode writeback on superblocks without data-integrity guarantees by only triggering flusher threads and returning early.
intent_record.what: A new early-return conditional was added to sync_inodes_sb() that checks whether sb->s_iflags has SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY set; if so, it calls wakeup_flusher_threads_bdi(bdi, WB_REASON_SYNC) and returns before the existing WARN_ON and subsequent sync wait logic.
intent_record.how: At runtime, filesystems marked with SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY no longer go through the normal synchronous inode writeback completion path in sync_inodes_sb(). Instead, the function only triggers writeback and exits immediately, avoiding waiting for writeout completion on filesystems that cannot guarantee data persistence from sync anyway.

intent_record.intent_summary: Always mark FUSE file inode mappings as having no data integrity while keeping the writeback deadlock flag conditional on writeback cache.
intent_record.what: The change removes braces from the `if (fc->writeback_cache)` block and moves `mapping_set_no_data_integrity(&inode->i_data);` out of that conditional so that only `mapping_set_writeback_may_deadlock_on_reclaim(&inode->i_data);` remains guarded.
intent_record.how: `mapping_set_no_data_integrity()` is now always applied when initializing a FUSE file inode, regardless of whether writeback caching is enabled, while the writeback deadlock-on-reclaim flag is still set only when `fc->writeback_cache` is true.

intent_record.intent_summary: Mark FUSE superblocks with SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY so the kernel does not assume data integrity support for FUSE mounts.
intent_record.what: A new statement was added in fuse_sb_defaults() to set the superblock internal flag SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY via `sb->s_iflags |= SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY;` alongside the existing s_iflags defaults.
intent_record.how: At runtime, newly initialized FUSE superblocks are now explicitly marked as not providing data integrity guarantees, causing the kernel to treat these mounts accordingly and preventing assumptions that FUSE-backed filesystems support verified data integrity.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a new internal superblock flag to identify filesystems that cannot guarantee data persistence on sync.
intent_record.what: A new internal superblock flag macro, SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY, with value 0x00008000, was added to struct super_block flag definitions in fs_super_types.h, along with a comment stating that the filesystem cannot guarantee data persistence on sync.
intent_record.how: This introduces a new internal capability/state bit that filesystems or VFS code can set and test at runtime to mark superblocks where sync does not ensure durable data persistence, enabling later logic to treat such filesystems differently or avoid assuming normal data-integrity guarantees.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the obsolete `AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY` mapping flag from `mapping_flags`.
intent_record.what: The enum entry `AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY = 11` and its comment `/* no data integrity guarantees */` were removed from `enum mapping_flags`.
intent_record.how: This eliminates the `AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY` mapping flag from the codebase, preventing code from using that flag value and indicating that this flag is no longer part of the supported mapping flag definitions.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove obsolete inline helpers for the AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY address_space flag.
intent_record.what: Two static inline helper functions were removed: mapping_set_no_data_integrity(), which set the AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY flag in mapping->flags, and mapping_no_data_integrity(), which tested that same flag.
intent_record.how: This eliminates the local inline interfaces for setting and querying the AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY mapping flag, so code can no longer use these helpers from this header and must rely on other mechanisms or no longer support this flag path here; the runtime effect is removal of these helper entry points rather than addition of new behavior.

consistency_review.core_intent: Propagate and honor a no-data-integrity capability for FUSE and related writeback paths so the kernel avoids assuming synchronous data-integrity guarantees on FUSE-backed storage.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly modifies `wait_sb_inodes()` writeback waiting behavior for mappings lacking data-integrity semantics, which is part of the flawed sync/writeback handling described in the root cause.

The changes directly address the root cause by moving no-data-integrity handling to the superblock/filesystem level and making sync_inodes_sb() avoid the flusher/wait path for filesystems like FUSE that cannot guarantee synchronous data integrity.

The vulnerability stems from lacking a superblock-level way to mark filesystems that cannot provide sync data-integrity guarantees, causing the sync path to wait on flusher completion anyway. Adding a new internal superblock flag directly addresses that missing model.

The vulnerability stems from the obsolete per-inode `AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY` model being inadequate for the sync path. Removing `AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY` directly targets that root-cause mechanism rather than being a mere refactor.

This change only removes obsolete inline helper functions for the AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY flag. It does not modify the sync/writeback waiting logic in sync_inodes_sb() or the flusher-thread completion behavior that caused the vulnerability.

candidates.rationale: This conditional begins the logic that skips waiting on certain inode mappings during sync. It is part of the per-inode no-data-integrity handling that contributed to the incorrect sync semantics.

This is the direct vulnerable check: it models no-data-integrity at the mapping/inode level and causes wait_sb_inodes() to skip waiting for those mappings, while the earlier superblock-wide flusher wait still occurs, creating the mismatch described in the root cause.
This statement enforces the buggy behavior by skipping the inode writeback wait entirely once mapping_no_data_integrity(mapping) is true.

This line marks only FUSE inode mappings as lacking data-integrity guarantees. The root cause is that such state was tracked per-inode rather than at the superblock level, which led sync_inodes_sb() to still perform the superblock-wide flusher wait.

This hunk shows the pre-fix superblock setup lacking any SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY marking for FUSE. While not itself a buggy conditional, it reflects the missing superblock-level modeling that allowed sync_inodes_sb() to assume data-integrity-capable semantics.

vuln_statements.explanation: This check is the core of the bug: it models lack of data-integrity support at the mapping/inode level and causes wait_sb_inodes() to exclude such mappings from inode writeback waiting, while sync_inodes_sb() still performs the earlier superblock-wide flusher wait. That mismatch produced the incorrect sync behavior for FUSE and similar filesystems.

This statement operationalizes the faulty per-inode no-data-integrity logic by skipping the wait for the inode's writeback entirely once mapping_no_data_integrity(mapping) is true, directly contributing to the inconsistent sync semantics.

This line marks FUSE as no-data-integrity only at the inode mapping level. That encoding was the root modeling mistake: sync_inodes_sb() still treated the superblock as if flusher-thread completion waiting was appropriate, causing the vulnerable mismatch.
